header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 09:30 - 10:32 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai; Jared Liu; Maria Gonzalez; Owen Park; Lina Roy
Location: Zoom
Notes: Internal roadmap/launch readiness sync focusing on v2 kernel rollout, dedicated capacity, observability and rollback plans
summary: Quick sync to confirm readiness for the v2 kernel rollout next week. Primary concerns: latency regressions in long-context, observability/trace retention, canary rollback steps, and coordinating dedicated capacity for peak traffic. Agreed action items and deadlines; follow-ups scheduled.
topics: v2 kernel performance and latency tests
Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscale policies
Incident review: recent KV-cache miss spike
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: alright, uh good morning everyone, thanks for joining, quick check-in on the roadmap launch readiness for v2 kernel, I know we have a long list but want to make sure we cover blockers.
[00:22] Jared: yeah, thanks Priya, I only have about ten minutes of heavy stuff, I'll start with the perf numbers, so in staging we ran the 95th percentile latency tests with 16k context and we saw a 12 to 18% increase compared to v1 on some workloads, but throughput improved for shorter sequences. There's some noise, probably from the new attention kernel in combination with quantization.
[00:47] Maria: mm-hmm, I saw those graphs, and there was that one KV-cache miss spike last night where retention TTLs caused a flush — I think the miss rate went up when we hit a small GC window on the orchestrator. We correlated it to a segfault in one of the prefetch threads but it's intermittent.
[01:12] Owen: right, the prefetch thread issue is reproducible at high batch sizes, I'm working on a fix but it's a bit subtle with the async cache invalidation. I have a branch with a safer lock but need to run end-to-end to make sure it doesn't blow up latency elsewhere.
[01:37] Priya: okay so immediate question, is this a release blocker or can the canary handle it?
[01:45] Maria: I think it's canaryable, but we have to limit the canary to lower concurrent users and enable stricter circuit breakers. Also we should add a specific alert for KV-cache miss rate and prefetch thread errors.
[02:06] Jared: Agreed, and on the perf side we can tune the batcher to prefer smaller batches for long-context flows. That reduces throughput but keeps 95th down. We should document the tradeoff for product.
[02:28] Lina: can I ask a quick question — what's the impact on cost if we run smaller batch sizes? I need numbers for the GTM deck.
[02:35] Owen: ballpark, smaller batches will increase token-per-second cost by ~8-15% depending on mix, but we'll have fewer tail latency spikes. We can run a cost matrix and embed that into the launch playbook.
[02:55] Priya: good. Next, observability — Maria, you mentioned retention and traces?
[03:02] Maria: yeah, currently traces in staging are 7 days, which isn't enough for the post-launch raid when we need to triage regressions. We propose 30 days for traces for staging and 90 days for prod for first two weeks. Also increase Prometheus histogram buckets for request duration. Might need approval for storage.
[03:25] Jared: storage costs will spike, but it's worth it for the first two weeks. Can we compress or sample?
[03:30] Maria: we can sample low-priority traces and keep full fidelity for error traces. There's also the option to use our cold storage S3 bucket and keep indices in hot store for 14 days.
[03:46] Priya: add that as an action item, Maria to propose exact retention/poicy and cost estimate.
[03:52] Maria: noted.
[03:55] [04:00] Priya: rollback strategy — Owen?
[04:05] Owen: plan A is quick-fallback to v1 model on the same serving infra, with automated routing switch at the load-balancer. Plan B is scale-down of v2 nodes and shift traffic, and plan C is full revert of deployment artifacts. We need a script to do the routing change within 90 seconds. I can script that and test in staging.
[04:28] Jared: we'll also need to ensure KV cache warming for v1 when switching back. There's a warmup script we can run to prefill prefix caches.
[04:37] Owen: yes, I'll include warmup steps. Also, make sure the canary policy has a manual abort threshold at 5% error increase or 20% latency regression at p95.
[04:52] Priya: sounds reasonable. GTM coordination — Lina, are you blocked for materials?
[04:58] Lina: mostly good, I need the final SLO numbers and cost impact table. If engineering can share the cost matrix and canary thresholds by EOD Monday, marketing can finalize the launch page and customer comms.
[05:14] Priya: action: Jared and Owen to produce cost matrix and canary thresholds, send to Lina.
[05:20] Jared: okay.
[05:22] [05:30] Priya: quick incident review — the KV-cache miss spike last week, Maria you said it was a GC window. Can we get a postmortem doc?
[05:38] Maria: yes, I started a short postmortem, initial root cause is 1) prefetch thread race under high batch, 2) orchestrator GC plus library upgrade mismatch. I'll finish doc and propose mitigations: lock fix, backoff on prefetch, and upgrade coordination.
[05:56] Owen: one nuance — the particular python extension we use for prefetch behaves differently under our newer kernel, so we need a compatibility test in CI.
[06:07] Jared: I'll add a pre-merge CI test for the extension with the v2 kernel config.
[06:12] Priya: great. Anything else on incident?
[06:15] Maria: just that we need better alerting; I proposed an alert rule to page on sustained KV miss > 2% for 5 minutes.
[06:24] Priya: okay that's an action for you.
[06:27] [06:30] Priya: timeline check — final canary start is scheduled for 2026-12-23 at 00:00 UTC, with a 48-hour monitoring window and then scale on 2026-12-25 if all green. Is everyone aligned?
[06:45] Jared: aligned, but we should move earlier if tests finish. I'll aim for the 23rd.
[06:52] Owen: same.
[06:54] Lina: marketing can shift but needs the final numbers by 12/21 at latest.
[07:01] Priya: okay, decisions: proceed with canary on 12/23, extend staging trace retention to 30 days, implement prefetch lock fix and CI tests, and add rollback script. Next steps documented in the action items.
[07:17] [07:20] Priya: any risks or open concerns?
[07:22] Owen: long-context p95 regression is still the top risk; might require more tuning post-canary.
[07:28] Maria: alert noise during the garbage collection windows could cause false positives; we'll tune thresholds.
[07:33] Jared: dependency on the kernel vendor for one optimization could slip. I've pinged the vendor but keep it as a risk.
[07:41] Priya: ok please add vendor slack thread link in the doc.
[07:44] Owen: will do.
[07:46] [07:50] Lina: I'll put together the GTM runbook and send to the channel once I have the metrics.
[07:55] Priya: great. final recap — I'll compile the checklist, send it out, and set a follow-up on Monday to review pre-canary tests. Thanks everyone.
[08:10] Jared: thanks.
[08:12] Maria: thanks.
[08:14] Owen: bye.
[08:15] Lina: bye.
